sentences.text:
The dependents who are the wife and the major son, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation fixed by the Tribunal have filed this appeal challenging the award passed by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (II Court of Small Causes), Chennai in M.C.O.P.No.744 of 2016 dated 07.11.2022.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (II Court of Small Causes), Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The deceased Ezhumalai was walking at GST Road on 12.02.2016 and near the Vandalur Zoo bus stop at about 23.15 hours, a Tata Indigo car owned by the 1st respondent was driven in a rash and negligent manner and it dashed on the deceased and as a result, the deceased sustained grievious injuries and he sccumbed to the injuries.
It is under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed before the Tribunal.

3. The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence came to a conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1247 of 2024 negligent driving on the part of the offending vehicle.
Having rendered such a finding, the Tribunal proceeded to fix the compensation and the total compensation was fixed at Rs.10,96,000/- under various heads

as follows :-
Sl. Compensation awarded under Amount No. the head (in Rs.)
1. Loss of dependency Rs.9,75,000/-
2. Loss of Consortium Rs. 88,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
Total Rs.10,96,000/-
The above compensation was directed to be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.
6. The claimant not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation fixed by the Tribunal has filed this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

7. Heard Mr.C.Munusamy, learned counsel for appellants/claimants and Mr.T.K.Prem Kumar, learned counsel for 2nd respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1247 of 2024 8.

This Court carefully considered the submissions made on either side and the materials available E.Muthulakshmi vs Mj Mohamed Mansoor on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152018769/
2 on record.
9.
This Court also carefully went through the award passed by the Tribunal.

10. The only issue that was campaigned before this Court was with regard to the fixation of the monthly notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month and also the deduction of  towards the personal expenditure of the deceased.
11. As per the claimants, the deceased was a Chef and he was earning Rs.500/- per day.

However,
the avocation of the deceased and the monthly income earned by him was not substantiated before the Tribunal.

Therefore, the Tribunal proceeded to fix the monthly notional income at Rs.10,000/-
per month.
25% was added towards future prospects, since the age of the deceased was determined as 49 years.

12. The accident had taken place in the year 2016 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1247 of 2024 considering the fact that the deceased was a Chef and he was taking care of his wife and son, this Court finds that the notional monthly income of Rs.10,000/- is on the lower side.
Therefore, this Court is inclined to enhance the same by Rs.12,500/-.

If 25% is added towards future prospects, the total works out to Rs. 15,625/- [12500 + 25% future prospects]
13.
The Tribunal while dealing with the deduction towards personal expenses has taken note of the judgement of Sarla Varma.
While discussing, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that 1/3rd income must be deducted towards the personal expenses.
However, while calculating the loss of income, the Tribunal proceeded to deduct  towards personal expenses.
14. In Sarla varma case, the Apex Court indicated that deduction of  will arise in a case where a bachelor lost his life leaving behind his parents.
If the person is married and there are siblings, the Apex Court has indicated that the deduction towards personal expenses can only be 1/3 rd and not .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1247 of 2024 15.

In the light of the above discussion, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is calculated as follows :-
 Monthly notional income Rs. 12,500/-
 Add 25% future prospects Rs. 3,125/-
 Rs. 15,625/-
 Loss of dependency =Rs.15,625 x 12 x 13 x 2/3  = Rs.16,25,052/-
 (Rounded off to Rs.16,25,000/-)
16.

Insofar as the compensation that was fixed by the Tribunal under the other heads, this Court finds that a reasonable compensation has been fixed and it does not require the interference of this E.Muthulakshmi vs Mj Mohamed Mansoor on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152018769/
3 Court.
17.

In the light of the above discussion, this Court modifies the compensation in the following manner:
Sl.No.
Compensation
awarded
under Amount the head (in Rs.)

1. Loss of dependency Rs.16,25,000/-
2. Loss of Consortium Rs. 88,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/-
 Total Rs.17,46,00  18.
The compensation awarded by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1247 of 2024 Rs.10,96,000/- is enhanced to Rs.17,46,000/-.

The Insurance company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation, less the amount already deposited, together with interest at 7.5% p.a.
from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment.

Insofar as the enhanced compensation of Rs.6,50,000/- is concerned, the appellant/claimant will not be entitled for interest for the period of delay of 182 days as was ordered by this Court in C.M.P.No.1516 of 2024, dated 10.04.2024.
Insofar as the enhanced compensation is concerned, the deficit court fee, if not paid, shall be paid by the appellant.
The other directions issued by the Tribunal with regard to the mode of payment of compensation remains unaltered.
In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed in the above terms.
No costs.
